title: Filling the Void: Data-Driven Machine Learning-based Reconstruction of Sampled Spatiotemporal Scientific Simulation Data
problem: High-performance computing systems face a widening gap between compute performance and I/O capabilities, limiting storage of large-scale simulations that generate massive spatiotemporal data. Existing analysis lacks methods to effectively reconstruct complete datasets from intelligently sampled outputs.
motivation: Enabling high-fidelity reconstruction of complete spatiotemporal simulation data from sparse samples allows scientists to recover spatial and temporal detail without requiring prohibitive storage infrastructure.
method: The approach trains neural networks on sparsely sampled simulation output to reconstruct full-scale datasets. It uses pretraining and fine-tuning strategies to balance sampling rates, model training time, and reconstruction speed. The models demonstrate knowledge transfer to unseen timesteps and grid resolutions, outperforming Delaunay triangulation-based linear interpolation in quality, speed, and generalization.
key_novelty: Using neural networks trained on intelligently sampled data for spatiotemporal reconstruction with demonstrated generalization to unseen timesteps and grid resolutions.
contributions: Machine learning-based approach for reconstructing full-scale simulation datasets from sparsely sampled outputs
Strategies balancing sampling rates, model training overhead, and reconstruction time
Demonstration of knowledge transfer to unseen timesteps and grid resolutions
Empirical comparison showing superiority over Delaunay triangulation in reconstruction quality and speed
primary_theme: ML-based spatiotemporal reconstruction from sparse HPC simulation samples
